measures.title: Legislative Referendum 379: Judicial Nominating Commission
measures.summary: Referred by the Legislature (HJR 1024), this constitutional amendment restructures the 15-member Judicial Nominating Commission, which screens applicants for appellate and some trial judgeships. The governor and the Oklahoma Bar Association would each appoint six members (one from each current congressional district), and at least eight of those members would choose three at-large members; any number of commissioners could be licensed attorneys. It also changes term lengths, removes party-membership limits for the governor's and at-large appointees, lets commissioners serve consecutive terms, and drops the bar on commissioners' immediate family practicing law.
measures.yesMeans: You approve changing how Judicial Nominating Commission members are chosen, who may serve, and how long they serve, as described in the ballot title.
measures.noMeans: You reject the amendment, and the commission keeps its current structure based on the 1967 congressional districts and current membership rules.

measures.title: Legislative Referendum 381: Real property valuation
measures.summary: Referred by the Legislature (SJR 39), this constitutional amendment lowers the yearly cap on increases in a property's taxable fair cash value starting in tax year 2027: from 5% to 4% for most real property, and from 3% to 1.75% for homesteads and agricultural land. It also replaces the 'senior freeze' for homeowners 65 and older: instead of a full freeze for those under an income limit, increases would be capped at 1.75% a year, reduced to 1.4%, 1.05%, 0.7%, 0.35% or 0% depending on household income compared with the area median income set by HUD.
measures.yesMeans: You approve lowering the annual caps on property value increases and replacing the senior valuation freeze with an income-based sliding cap.
measures.noMeans: You reject the amendment, and the current 5% and 3% caps and the current senior valuation freeze stay in place.
